overall.summary: Every stated number, threshold, direction and subgroup reproduces and coverage and function preservation hold; the sodium U is described with a 'steeper low arm' and a 'slight' direct tilt that are only partly right, and smoking's 'wider' gate is the same parallel shift.

findings.statement: U-shaped risk in serum sodium, with a steeper low arm ... On the logit the low arm is the steeper: the score is 9.11 at 126 and 7.08 at 154, against -2.28 at the bottom
findings.check: probe the typical patient, sodium swept 126 to 154; compare the arms at equal distance from the bottom (139)
findings.evidence: The numbers reproduce (score 9.110 at 126, 7.081 at 154, -2.278 at 139) and once open the low arm is steeper per mmol/L (about 1.8 logit per mmol/L below 133 against 0.79 above 139). But the high arm opens right at the bottom (139 to 140) while the low arm opens only below 133, so near the normal range the high side rises much faster: 6 mmol/L below the bottom (133) the score is -1.35 (risk 20.6%), 6 mmol/L above (145) it is +1.36 (risk 79.6%). Inside the 1st-99th percentile range the U is close to symmetric in risk: 96.2% at 129 (10 below) and 96.3% at 148 (9 above). 'Steeper low arm' holds only for the slope once the arm is open and for the end-to-end range, not for the shape a reader would picture.

findings.statement: a U-shaped response to serum sodium (lowest predicted risk near 139 mmol/L for the typical patient, with a steeper low arm that smokers enter at a higher sodium)
findings.check: same sodium sweep as V1
findings.evidence: Lowest risk at 139 (9.3%) and smokers entering the low arm at a higher sodium (gate on at 134 for a smoker, 132 for a non-smoker) reproduce. 'Steeper low arm' is only partly right: near the bottom the high arm rises faster (risk 79.6% at 145 against 20.6% at 133 for the typical non-smoker); the same wording in record.overall_function and in risk_model's hypothesis carries the same caveat.

findings.statement: sodium's direct edge (weight -0.631 per sd, in direct_terms) tilts the U slightly downwards with rising sodium
findings.check: direct_terms contribution across the sodium sweep (typical patient)
findings.evidence: The weight reproduces (-0.6305 per sd; sd 4.09 mmol/L), but the tilt is not slight: the direct term changes the logit by about 2.9 across the 1st-99th percentile range (129 to 148) and by 0.93 across the flat bottom 133 to 139, where it is the only thing moving the risk (20.6% to 9.3%). The floor of the U is a downward slope ending at a corner where the high arm opens.

findings.statement: Smoking therefore raises the sodium level at which the gate opens and makes it open wider (value 2.78 for a smoker against 2.01 for a non-smoker at sodium 128)
findings.check: node 228 value and pre-activation for smokers and non-smokers, sodium swept
findings.evidence: The values reproduce (2.785 vs 2.010), but smoking is a single parallel shift: the gate's pre-activation is higher by 0.775 at every open sodium value (2.785-2.010 at 128, 1.062-0.288 at 132, 3.646-2.872 at 126), with the same slope. 'Opens wider' is the same shift seen at one sodium, not a second effect; record.overall_function's 'shifts to higher sodium and widens' reads as two effects.

low_sodium_smoker_gate.why: A hyponatraemia detector that the model confirms: off above 133 mmol/L for a non-smoker, steeply rising below, opening about 2 mmol/L higher in smokers.

high_sodium_hinges.why: The hypernatraemia arm: both hinges switch on at 140 mmol/L and rise in a straight line, matching an outcome rate of 98.7% above 145; one hinge also carries a fitted noise input.

bmi_hinge.why: A clean hinge on BMI above about 27 kg/m2, correctly described as almost unused (AUC unchanged when removed).

low_hr_hinge.why: A slow-heart-rate hinge below about 77 beats/min whose two roles (own negative term, damping the pressure chain) reproduce; its net effect is only readable at the composition.

sbp_chain.why: Three serial pressure hinges whose own terms make high pressure look protective; that reading is part-level only and is reversed by the gate for slow hearts, so the leaf's domain meaning exists only inside bp_hr_interaction.

bp_hr_gate.why: A gate open when systolic pressure is high relative to heart rate (sbp minus heart rate scores 0.97; shock index 0.91), shut by a fast heart or low sodium, as stated.

direct_terms.why: A linear risk score of eight inputs; age, creatinine and diabetes readings are clear, but the sum as a whole has no single reading (best concept 0.66).
